newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- The Securities and Exchange Commission charged CS First Boston Corp of CS Holding with securities fraud in connection with underwriting pension funds for Orange County, Calif.
- U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig set a new rule to make it easier for banks to offer additional financial products.
- Although the stock prices of computer makers are rising, those of computer retailers are not.
- Home Access Health and Direct Access Diagnostics of Johnson & Johnson are trying to figure out how best to market their respective products that allow people to conduct their own HIV test.
- The United States had a trade deficit with China that was larger in September than any other held with another country.
- Brokerage firm Smith Barney is struggling with complaints of sexual discrimination from some female employees.
- The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission wants to participate in the negotiations to settle the racial discrimination suit against Texaco Inc.
- Kmart Corp reported its second straight profitable quarter.
- The Treasury Department will publish a draft report on Thursday that outlines the government's opposition to new federal taxes on the Internet.
- Chiroscience Group Plc has agreed to acquire Darwin Molecular Corp.
- Former presidential candidate Bob Dole has agreed to appear in a commercial for Air France.
- The rail tunnel under the English Channel might stay closed until the end of the week as a result of a fire.
